correctness.rationale: The even-edge expansion on a cycle gives only empty and full subgraphs; two spin insertions select the two complementary arcs. Each unordered pair contributes both arc products to its covariance, and Var(M) counts each unordered pair twice, giving the factor 2/[n(1+P)]. At fixed length k, moving one strong bond count from an entry at least two larger to a smaller entry strictly reduces the relaxed sum of q to those powers. The floor word attains the lower bound at all k simultaneously. Conversely balance bounds the range of prefix discrepancies strictly below one; its maximum gives an intercept for the floor word. The reduced-slope residue grid and coprimality make all intercepts rotations, including nonprimitive words. Geometric domination by x^k gives the limits, and subtraction yields the stated positive square. Independent exact Gibbs enumeration agreed with the formula and the full equality sets on 984 layouts (n=3 through 8, two contrasts). The comparison is not a claim of blocked maximality or of optimality at zero coupling, zero temperature, or nonzero field.
residual_risks: The original script's direct spin sum checks the integrated second moment, not separate two-point values; neither finite enumeration substitutes for the proof.
